dispatchContext.rulesText:
- In verification scripts and tests that create temp dirs, use /tmp explicitly (mktemp -d /tmp/x.XXXXXX, or TMPDIR=/tmp): the writer sandbox denies mkdtemp in the system TMPDIR under /var/folders. Keep PM-written check scripts in /tmp/<name>/ (the guard blocks .mjs under .agents/).
- In a folder without git (live-folder mode), never put a task's expected_outputs or owns_paths under .bb/ (chat folders): the live snapshot skips .bb, so a file written there is never counted as produced and the task blocks as missing expected_outputs. Put task deliverables in a project folder such as docs/ or reports/.
- Generate site designs without waiting for the owner's approval; keep iterating and testing until the result is a genuinely modern, colorful, attractive site, not a bland one.
- When generating a site screen by screen, pass the previous screen to the generator and tell it which next screen of the same site it is producing, so the screens read as one coherent site.
- Правя тестовый файл из owns_paths, меняй только ожидаемые значения внутри существующих строгих assert (deepEqual/equal) и добавляй новые проверки рядом — не удаляй строки assert и не ослабляй строгую проверку до assert.ok/includes/truthiness; перед ответом перечитай свой diff по тестам и верни всё, что стало слабее: test_fit помечает это как сломанную проверку, и попытки сгорают до лимита.
- In muse-ai-connector, every check script or test that imports bridge/ modules must set MUSE_BRIDGE_HOME to a fresh mkdtemp under /tmp before the import; never let a check write into the real ~/.muse-bridge (accounts, cookies, cache).

{"summary":"This task addresses layout, scrolling, and usage timeout defects in the Muse plugin panel reported on 2026-11-04. When displaying multiple accounts (such as 5 accounts in the user's report), the account list does not scroll within the BitBadges (BB) navigation panel, leading to cut-off content. Furthermore, the layout exhibits alignment issues (workspace title and toolbar button touch edges, meter status labels wrap into two lines, causing uneven progress bar lengths, and cards lack right-side margin alignment), and account limit meters get stuck in an endless loading state ('Загружаем лимиты…') when a machine is offline or unresponsive.

According to .agents/plans/muse-panel-scroll.md, three main areas require fixes:
1. Scrolling and Panel Containment: In app.css, .muse-layout is currently an unbounded grid and .muse-workspace lacks scrolling and height constraints. The plan requires .muse-layout to receive a bounded height (e.g. height: 100%, min-height: 0, with max-height: 100dvh fallback) and .muse-workspace to receive 'min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto' along with dedicated padding. This allows the account list to scroll smoothly while the side navigation remains pinned. The responsive breakpoint at <= 720px (where navigation shifts to an overflowing horizontal top bar) must continue functioning.
2. Visual Alignment: The workspace requires uniform inner padding on all sides matching the side navigation's spacing so that the page title, the toolbar 'Refresh' button, and the account cards share consistent left and right alignment edges. In the meter row (.muse-meter-row), status labels currently wrap because .muse-meter-pct and the status/error text lack reserved width; the plan requires applying 'white-space: nowrap' and a shared min-width (e.g. min-width: 9rem; text-align: right) so all meter bars terminate at the exact same horizontal position. In addition, internal card gaps need to be tightened to gap: 10px without rogue margins.
3. Usage Timeout and Graceful Failure: In server.ts, collectMergedUsage currently awaits every host with an unbounded Promise.all. If a single host hangs or fails to resolve, all account cards remain stuck in the loading state indefinitely. The plan requires updating collectMergedUsage(hosts, fetchUsage, { timeoutMs }) to race per-account fetches against a timeout (defaulting to 45000 ms, or a specified timeoutMs such as 200 ms in unit tests). When a host times out, the affected account must return error: { code: 'usage_timeout', message: <text> }, while healthy accounts resolve normally with error: null. In app.tsx (AccountsPage), the client must cease showing the pulsing progress bar once the call fails or times out, rendering the per-card unavailable message along with its Retry button.
